name: profile.py
summary: Django REST Framework ModelSerializer that mediates between Profile model instances and JSON representations for the users API.
purpose: Decouples the internal Profile database schema from external API consumers by handling serialization, deserialization, and validation of profile data in a centralized, reusable component.
responsibilities: Serialize Profile model instances into JSON for API responses
Deserialize and validate incoming JSON payloads for profile creation and updates
Enforce field-level and object-level validation rules
Control field exposure to prevent leaking internal or sensitive model attributes
Bridge the users domain model with the REST API presentation layer
inputs: Profile model instance or QuerySet for serialization
Optional request context for conditional field handling
outputs: JSON-compatible primitive data structures for API responses
Validated Python dictionaries ready for model creation or update
Created or updated Profile model instances
architecture_notes: Acts as a Data Transfer Object (DTO) within the Django REST Framework layered architecture. Inheriting from ModelSerializer (implied by imports) auto-generates fields from the Profile model, reducing boilerplate but requiring explicit Meta field declarations to avoid over-exposure. Located in backend/apps/users/serializers/ to enforce separation of concerns between data access (models), business logic (views), and API presentation (serializers).
improvements: Explicitly declare Meta.fields instead of '__all__' to prevent accidental exposure of sensitive internal fields
Add type hints to custom methods and override signatures for better static analysis
Split into ProfileReadSerializer and ProfileWriteSerializer if read/write representations diverge
Implement custom validate_<field> methods for complex business rules (e.g., image size, bio length)
Add select_related/prefetch_related optimization hints or use a dedicated service layer for heavy profile queries
